Write the branch support table and annotated reference tree

Source: R/branch-support.R
write_branch_support.Rd

Export the two Support outputs already computed by align_branches(). Each row describes one original reference branch. An internal branch is eligible for a gene when its projected split belongs to it alone and retains at least two taxa on each side. Support is the number recovered divided by the number eligible, irrespective of branch lengths. Numeric internal labels in the Newick tree give percentages. A percentage of zero is printed as 0. A branch with no eligible genes has an NA percentage and an empty tree label. If the display root divides one internal branch, both halves show its label. The table uses R's primitive coordinate_id labels. n_dec counts eligible genes and n_rec counts recoveries. Match coordinate_id against the result's primitive_coordinates to look up the taxon split.

Usage

write_branch_support(result, output_dir)

Arguments

result

A single fixed- or free-mode result returned by align_branches().

output_dir

A new directory in an existing parent directory.

Value

Invisibly, the named paths to support.tsv (table) and support.nwk (tree).

Examples

genes <- c(same = "((A,B),(C,D));", different = "((A,C),(B,D));")
result <- align_branches("((A,B),(C,D));", genes)
result$support_newick
#> [1] "((A,B)50,(C,D)50);"
destination <- tempfile()
paths <- write_branch_support(result, destination)
readLines(paths[["tree"]])
#> [1] "((A,B)50,(C,D)50);"
unlink(destination, recursive = TRUE)
